chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Al-Hakam Al-Khayyat, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'I contract to tailor a garment for one dirham, and I hand it over to the client for more than that, increasing only for the cutting/sewing.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'There is no problem with it.' Then he (peace be upon him) said, 'There is no problem in what you contract as work, then you increase the price in it.'

key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: There is no problem/it is permissible

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to charge more for tailoring than the initial agreed price?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* clarifies the permissibility of *al-istifdal* (increasing the price) in service contracts, a key concept in Shia commercial jurisprudence (*Fiqh al-Mu'amalat*). Imam al-Sadiq (AS) validates that once a worker accepts a task, they may charge a higher rate for the completed work, provided the initial acceptance was valid and the increase reflects the actual value or effort expended, rather than mere speculation. This ruling underscores the flexibility in Islamic contracts to accommodate market dynamics and individual merit, distinguishing it from *gharar* (uncertainty) when the scope of work is clear.

en.hubeali: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Safwan, from Al Hakam Al Khayyat who said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘I hire the clothes (tailoring) for one Dirham and I submit these for more than that, not having increased upon it except for cutting it’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem with it’. Then he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem in what you contract from a work, then you improve in it’.
en.sarwar: 2. Abu Ali al-Ash’ariy has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Jabbar from Safwan from al-Hakam al-Khayyat who has said the following:

“Upon my asking abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a cloth (for tailoring) that I accept for a dirham and then give it to another person on credit for more than a dirham without doing anything more than cutting. He (the Imam) said, ‘It is not unlawful.’ He (the Imam) then said, ‘It is not unlawful if you accept a work then seek increase in it.’”
